 The Director will partner with Go-to-Market, Customer Success, Support, Finance, Legal and Partner Operations to simplify processes, strengthen data quality and controls, and improve how work gets done.  Own a business-aligned application roadmap and investment portfolio, balancing growth, operational efficiency, risk, user experience and technical debt. 
 Partner with functional leaders to define business problems, accountable process owners, funding, expected benefits and adoption commitments before delivery begins. 
 Run transparent prioritization and portfolio reviews; challenge low-value requests and communicate trade-offs, dependencies and decisions clearly.

 Build a prioritized portfolio of AI and automation opportunities across business workflows, starting with process redesign and data readiness rather than tool selection. 
 Lead build-versus-buy-versus-configure decisions with Enterprise AI Engineering, application owners, Security, Legal and Finance.

title: Growth Manager, Customer Expansion
description:
About  Engine   
  Engine  is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade,  Engine  has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on  Engine 's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents.  That work has earned  Engine  recognition as TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), a spot on Inc.'s Power Partners list (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).  We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.  Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us. 
  Why this role matters   Engine  is the travel and spend management platform transforming how businesses move. We're cash flow positive, scaling rapidly, and backed by Telescope Partners, Blackstone, and Permira — and our goal to double revenue in 2027 is the most ambitious target we've ever set. Getting there isn't only about winning new logos. Some of the most efficient growth we have is already inside the building.  More than 33,000 businesses and over 1 million travelers already book through  Engine . Many of them run only a fraction of their eligible travel spend on the platform, use a single product when they could use several, or manage travel separately across business units and sister organizations we haven't reached yet. The gap between what a customer does today and what they could represents massive surface area, and closing it costs a fraction of acquiring a net-new account.   This role owns that expansion motion end to end. More share of wallet, more products per account (Flights, Rental Cars, Flex/FlexPro,  Engine  X), more business units, more subsidiary and parent organizations. You'll build the systems, signals, and campaigns that turn 33,000 existing relationships into a compounding growth engine: working through our account management teams where accounts are managed, and building automated motions to reach the ones that aren't. The mandate is broad on purpose. If it grows an existing customer, it's in scope.  What you'll own  
 
 End-to-end ownership of growth-led expansion programs:  Strategy and execution of the marketing and growth programs (systems, signals, and campaigns) that drive expansion revenue across  Engine 's existing base. 
 
 Every expansion play:  Grow share of wallet by capturing more of each customer's travel and spend, cross-sell additional products, and expand into new business units. 
 
 Data-driven targeting and reach:  Combine firmographic data, internal customer spend, and in-app behavioral signals to decide who to reach, with what, and when. 
 
 Coordinated, multi-channel plays:  Partner with ABM and field/events to fold direct mail, gifting, and field events into the expansion motion. 
 
 Expansion accountability and reporting:  Own the numbers: expansion pipeline, share-of-wallet growth, cross-sell attach rates, net revenue retention contribution, and downstream impact. Deliver clean readouts to account management, growth, and executive leadership on what's working and what's not. 
  The problems you'll solve  This role sits at the intersection of data, messaging, and cross-functional execution. You'll be expected to ship fast, learn faster, and turn one-off expansion wins into repeatable programs. Some of the challenges you'll inherit:  
 
 Knowing which customers are ready to grow, and when:  With 33,000 customers, the hard part isn't finding expansion opportunities, it's prioritizing them. You'll turn spend, booking, and behavioral data into a clear signal for which accounts are ready and what to put in front of them. 
 
 Reaching the unmanaged base at scale:  Only a fraction of customers have a dedicated AM. You'll build automated motions that deliver relevant, well-timed expansion offers to everyone else, without letting personalization fall off a cliff. 
 
 Making 1:1 plays something the team actually runs:  A great expansion play that account managers don't use is worth nothing. You'll work directly with account management to understand the friction, fit the play to how they actually work, and close the loop between what the data says and what happens in the account. 
 
 Cross-selling without the noise:  More product isn't always the right pitch. You'll figure out which cross-sell offers genuinely fit an account's behavior (Flex/FlexPro,  Engine  X, Flights, Cars) and which just add noise, so expansion outreach earns attention instead of burning it. 
 
 Attributing expansion cleanly:  You'll build the measurement to separate campaign-driven expansion from organic growth.

title: Taxation and Compliance Specialist
description:
Job Summary:  We’re hiring a Senior Specialist in Tax and Corporate Compliance. In this role, you will own the company’s licensing, tax registration and corporate records across multiple US states and international jurisdictions. You will make sure every permit, filing and renewal stays active and in good standing.  The role needs someone who is organized and self-directed, and who can track hundreds of deadlines without missing one. You’ll work directly with Finance, outside counsel, state agencies and registered agents, and you’ll report monthly to leadership. It suits a part-qualified or qualified ACCA, CA, ICMA or ICSP professional who has worked in tax, compliance or company secretarial roles and is ready to take ownership of a full compliance function.   Key Responsibilities     Business Licenses & Registrations    
 Prepare, file and track new applications for state and local business licenses, foreign qualifications and DBAs. 
 Obtain and renew industry permits, including tobacco, cigarette, cigar and nicotine retailer, distributor, wholesaler and delivery-sale permits, along with any required bonds. 
 Keep entity records current with each Secretary of State, including annual reports and registered agent details. 
 Process changes of address, ownership, officers or business name with every affected agency. 
    Tax Registrations & Renewals    
 Register the company for sales and use tax, excise tax and other state tax accounts wherever there is nexus or taxable product sales. 
 Track renewal dates, file renewals on time and keep all permits active and in good standing. 
 Coordinate with Finance on filing frequency, account numbers and good-standing certificates. 
 Collect, issue and maintain resale and exemption certificates for customers and vendors. 
    Research & Compliance    
 Research licensing, tax and product regulations before the company enters a new state or launches a new product. 
 Monitor changes in law and agency rules, such as nicotine-pouch tax rulings, flavor bans, age-verification rules and PACT Act updates, and summarize what they mean for the business. 
 Maintain a state-by-state compliance matrix showing what’s required, what’s held and what’s outstanding. 
 Support audits, agency inquiries and investigations by gathering records under the direction of Finance and outside counsel. 
    Corporate Secretarial    
 Maintain corporate records, including formation documents, operating agreements, ownership records, and officer and member resolutions. 
 Prepare and track annual reports, beneficial ownership filings and good-standing certificates for each entity. 
 Draft routine resolutions, consents and minutes, and keep the corporate document repository organized. 
 Respond to KYC and due-diligence requests from banks, vendors and customers with accurate company documents. 
    Records & Process    
 Own a central license and tax register with permit numbers, effective and expiry dates, fees, contacts and copies. 
 Run a renewal calendar that sends reminders at least 90 days before each deadline. 
 Make sure physical permits are displayed where required and that old or voided permits are archived. 
 Manage relationships with state agencies, outside licensing vendors and registered agents. 
 Report monthly to leadership on status, risks and upcoming deadlines. 
    Finance & Accounting Support    
 Prepare and file sales and use tax and tobacco excise tax returns, and reconcile tax liabilities to the general ledger. 
 Support month-end close with account reconciliations, journal entries, accruals and prepaid schedules. 
 Assist with accounts payable and receivable, including vendor setup, invoice processing and payment runs. 
 Track and pay license fees, surety bonds and registered agent costs, and maintain the compliance budget. 
 Respond to tax notices and support external audits by preparing schedules and supporting documents. 
 Help with management reporting, ad hoc analysis and finance projects as assigned. 
  Requirements  
 ACCA, CA, CMA/ICMA or Chartered Secretary (ICSP or equivalent) qualification, either full or part-qualified. A degree in accounting, finance, commerce or law with strong relevant experience will also be considered. 
 At least 4 years of hands-on experience in tax, accounting, corporate compliance, company secretarial or regulatory filing work, for example at an audit or tax firm or in a corporate finance team. 
 Solid understanding of indirect taxes (sales tax, VAT or excise) and how tax registrations and filings work. 
 Proven experience with statutory filings and maintaining corporate records with government regulators. 
 Exceptional organization skills, with a track record of managing a high volume of deadlines accurately. 
 Excellent written and spoken English, and a clear, professional manner on calls and emails with government agencies. 
 Self-directed and a quick learner who can pick up a new regulatory system and work without close supervision.

description:
Description   MEDvidi  is an AI-powered mental healthcare clinic setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more.  MEDvidi ’s technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality.  As our   Product Manager for Insurance,   you’ll own an entirely new product line: bringing insurance payments to a platform that today runs almost entirely on self-pay. You’ll build eligibility, prior authorization, and claims into a business already handling ~18,000 visits a month, a genuine zero-to-one effort that opens a new revenue stream for the company.You’ll own the “coverage truth” (eligibility and benefits, the payer → plan → coverage data model, and cost-share), the economics of the insurance model, prior authorization flows, and the path from visit to claim to payment. You’ll work at the intersection of clinical, finance, engineering, and legal, partnering with a cross-functional pod of engineers and QA that will grow as the line scales.    Why this role:    
 
  Zero-to-one ownership.   You’re standing up an entire insurance product line from scratch inside a profitable, working telehealth business 
 
  Measured impact.   Your work opens a new revenue stream, and success is measured in insured visits paid at the expected rate, denial rate, and time to cash, not features shipped. 
 
  Breadth and real influence.   You’ll operate across clinical, finance, product, and engineering, owning the systems a dozen stakeholders depend on and driving the decisions that unblock launch. 
  Responsibilities  
 
  Own insurance as a product line.   The insurance team is the centre of product decisions for everything insurance touches. 
 
  Launch insurance end to end.   Map how insurance should work at  MEDvidi , prototype it, and validate it against real cases with revenue-cycle staff, coordinators and patients. Take every decision blocking launch to the people who own it, with a recommendation and a deadline, and coordinate the launch across teams and vendors. 
 
  Coverage.   Eligibility and benefits checks, the payer → plan → coverage data model, and cost-share (copay, deductible, coinsurance), so every booking gets a correct answer on coverage and on what the patient owes before the visit. 
 
  Patient money.   Estimates before the visit, collecting copay and deductible, balances after the payer adjudicates, statements, superbills for out-of-network patients, and the rules for when an insured patient can still pay cash. 
 
  Prior authorisation.   From prescription to medication in hand, plus visit authorisations where payers require them. 
 
  Visit to claim to payment.   With the team, build the full revenue-cycle loop: claims, clearinghouse, remittance, denials and appeals. 
    This role is not for you if:    
 You want a defined roadmap and clean requirements handed to you: here, the requirements don’t exist yet, and you build them from knowledge scattered across teams and vendors. 
 You think of the job as shipping features as specified, rather than owning a business outcome you can measure in money. 
 You wait for authority before you act, or you’re uncomfortable driving and escalating decisions with people who don’t report to you. 
  Requirements

description:

  ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen fast.   
 ZoomInfo has rebuilt itself around AI, and every agentic experience we ship runs on one shared platform — Copilot chat, agent teams, bots, GTM Studio, MarketingOS, and products that don't exist yet. As Senior Director of Product Management for the Agentic Platform, you'll be the right hand to our VP of Agents & Orchestration, owning the core primitives every agent depends on and the forward-looking R&D that keeps our agents ahead of what off-the-shelf models and frameworks can do. The best practices for agentic platforms are being written right now, and you'll help write them. 
  What You'll Do  
 
 You will set the multi-year Agentic Platform strategy and turn it into a roadmap that balances reliability, speed for product teams, and bets on the frontier. 
 You will own core platform primitives — multi-agent orchestration, planning and execution runtimes, memory and context management, tool and MCP infrastructure, guardrails, and observability — and define the abstractions that let product teams compose new agents quickly. 
 You will lead the product side of custom model training and fine-tuning on ZoomInfo's proprietary data, deciding where custom models create lasting advantage versus frontier models. 
 You will build the decisioning-model layer that lets agents choose the right action, partnering with data science to turn ZoomInfo's signals into models agents invoke as first-class capabilities. 
 You will run a structured orchestration R&D program that tracks emerging research and moves the winners into production. 
 You will identify and ship net-new platform capabilities that unlock new product surfaces and revenue, taking ideas from whiteboard sketch to production primitive. 
 You will partner with engineering to make agent infrastructure production-grade — measurable on execution at scale, latency, cost per task, security, and compliance. 
 You will build and grow a team of senior and principal PMs, hiring for technical depth and ownership and developing leaders who run their own areas with the same bar you hold. 
 
  What You Bring  
  Must-Have:  
 
 At least 10 years building technical products, including at least 3 years leading teams of PMs or running a company 
 Deep, hands-on experience with production agentic systems — agents that plan, invoke tools, and take real actions, not just chat interfaces 
 A track record of taking an AI or agentic product from 0→1, either as a founder or as the product leader who owned it end to end 
 Fluency across the modern agentic stack, including orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, or custom), MCP and tool-calling patterns, RAG and memory architectures, and evals and observability 
 Enough technical depth to review architecture docs, read agent traces, and prototype in code yourself 
 
  Preferred:  
 
 Working knowledge of model development, including fine-tuning, post-training, evaluation design, and the economics of custom versus frontier models 
 Experience building platform products where engineering and product teams are your customers 
 Experience shipping decisioning, ranking, or recommendation models into production 
 Experience in B2B, GTM, or data platform businesses
